answerCheck.reason: H(z)=R(z)-P(z)Q(z) has degree 6, because PQ has degree 5 and the leading degree-6 term of R cannot cancel. Thus H is nonconstant and the fundamental theorem of algebra gives at least one complex zero. For attainability choose P=z^2+1, Q=z^3+2, R=PQ+(z-1)^6. These have degrees 2,3,6 and constants 1,2,3. The equation becomes (z-1)^6=0, with only the distinct zero 1. Hence minimum N=1, B. The factor theorem alone bounds or checks roots but does not prove a nonconstant polynomial must have a complex zero.

routes.label: Construct one repeated zero with the required constant terms

answerCheck.reason: The nonzero constant term excludes zero roots. Degree 5 permits only one orbit {u, uω, uω²}, with u real. The nonreal conjugate roots have a common multiplicity k, so the multiplicities are (5-2k,k,k), giving only (3,1,1) and (1,2,2). In both cases the constant term is -u^5 = 2020, which fixes u uniquely. Both multiplicity patterns produce a valid real polynomial.

answerCheck.reason: The original denominator excludes all its real roots, even when a numerator factor cancels. In a nonpositive set [a,b] union (c,d), a<b<c<d, the closed endpoints a,b must be numerator zeros not excluded by the denominator, and the open endpoints c,d must be denominator zeros. All four endpoints belong to {1,2,3,4,5}. Monicity and degree3 then leave one extra factor in each polynomial. To preserve the required signs and endpoint types, these factors must be the same (x-t): otherwise one gains an extra sign boundary or isolated zero, or changes a prescribed endpoint type. Write P=(x-a)(x-b)(x-t), Q=(x-c)(x-d)(x-t). The choices t=c and t=d are always valid, and define exactly the same function on exactly the same natural domain R minus {c,d}; they must not be counted twice as functions. A third possibility is the unused fifth integer e, but only if its removable hole lies outside the required nonpositive set. This happens for unused e=1,3,5, and fails for e=2 or4 because that hole would cut one of the required intervals. There are five ordered endpoint quadruples, giving five base functions, plus three distinct additional-domain-hole functions, hence eight distinct natural-domain functions. If removable holes are entirely disregarded in function identity, the count instead becomes five; that convention also gives no listed option. The source13 counts polynomial-pair representations: two for each of the five endpoint quadruples plus the three allowable unused-root representations. For a concrete duplicate, (P,Q)=((x-1)(x-2)(x-3),(x-3)^2(x-4)) and ((x-1)(x-2)(x-4),(x-3)(x-4)^2) both define (x-1)(x-2)/((x-3)(x-4)) on R minus {3,4}, with nonpositive set [1,2] union (3,4). The exact certificate independently enumerates all35*35=1225 monic cubic pairs from root multisets, evaluates every real sign cell and root-domain point using rational arithmetic, and confirms13 eligible pairs,8 natural-domain function classes and5 reduced expressions. None of the listed choices is the function count under either stated convention.

answerCheck.reason: The polynomial is p(x^4), so its zeros satisfy x^4=2009, x^4=9002, or x^4=2009+9002πi. Each positive-real equation has two real and two nonreal roots; the nonreal right-hand side has four nonreal roots. All roots are distinct, giving 2+2+4=8 nonreal zeros.
